content:
Apple has announced this week that iOS 27 will officially launch for all users on Monday, September 14.

Additionally, the company said that two features from the iOS 27 beta have been removed and will be introduced later through a "future software update" for iPhone: the suggested functionality in Messages, and the automatic password changing feature.

Apple updated its website this week to reflect that these features have been temporarily removed from iOS 27. The relevant changes also apply to other operating systems, including iPadOS 27 and macOS 27. Reddit users earlier noticed that the automatic password changing feature was removed in iOS 27 beta 5, and Apple has now updated its website to confirm this change.

As a refresher, the suggested feature in the Messages app would let users add items to Reminders, Notes, or Calendar with one tap, based on the content of the conversation.

Below is Apple's description of the Passwords feature:

The Passwords app will attempt to directly visit websites where your password is weak or has been compromised, and automatically update the password. At WWDC, Apple explained that this feature uses Apple Intelligence and Safari, "on your behalf".

There are currently no further details on when these two features will return to iOS 27. Apple's website only states that they will be introduced in a "future software update".
